cohort: A total of 175 females presenting in labor at term were included in the study.
finding: The presence of meconium stained liquor in females presenting in labor at term was significantly associated with higher rates of C-section, poor Apgar scores, NICU admission, birth asphyxia, and early neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: The C-section rate was significantly higher among women with meconium stained liquor (37.3%) compared to those without (18.5%).
followup_time: 3 days (for maternal and early neonatal mortality observation)
